title: Crash debris analysed as aluminum and barium, matching Brown's Winterhaven proposal

tellings.quote: And where have we seen barium before? Both on the chalkboard at the Bownson labs where Townsend Brown worked and in his Winterhaven proposal. Brown brings up barium to be used in one of his motors for his gravitator discs.

plain: Debris from a crashed object was tested in the 1950s and found to be aluminum and barium, and barium also shows up in the work of the inventor Townsend Brown: written on a chalkboard at the labs where he worked, and in his Winterhaven proposal, a plan in which he meant to use barium in a motor for his "gravitator discs". Michels tells this himself in his documentary on Brown, citing a man named Michael Swords. He raises it because the match would tie the crash debris to Brown's own designs for flying craft.
